title: Parker avocado (NSIC Av 02): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Parker avocado: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Parker avocado is an avocado variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Parker is a registered avocado variety, also sold or known as NSIC Av 02. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 1995 as NSIC 1995 Av 02. Robert Parker bred it. Its record notes a yield of 500 to 700 fruits.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Av 02, this is the same avocado. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [avocado variety finder](/crop-varieties/avocado), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of 500 to 700 fruits.

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Parker was about 50 years old when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 500 to 700 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in Aug. Sept. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit avocado fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Parker weighs about 561.4 grams, and its shape is ovoid. The flesh is creamy yellow and smooth and firm. The edible part is 81 percent of the fruit. The registry notes its fruiting season as Aug. Sept, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Ovoid, about 560 g, purple, leathery skin, creamy yellow, firm flesh, buttery and nutty, about 81 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a very heavy bearing Laguna avocado: 500 to 700 fruits a tree. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Parker avocado

Grafted avocado bears sooner and true to type. Pick a selection by fruit size and flesh, and plant two kinds that flower at different times of day for better fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Av 02 the same as Parker?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Av 02 is another name for Parker, registered as NSIC 1995 Av 02. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 500 to 700 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Parker?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
